text:
Arseny Gritsyuk was a fifth-round pick in 2019 who spent years in the KHL before coming over, and in his second NHL season he's become a real part of a Devils team that has won eight of its last ten. He has 17 points in 21 games on under 16 minutes a night, and New Jersey owns nearly 60% of the shot attempts and expected goals at five on five when he's out.

Some of it is running hot. He has eight goals on 5.1 expected, shooting 17% after 9% last season, and his line has scored six more goals than its chances. His 3.1 points per 60 sits well above our talent range of 1.8 to 2.6. The goals have already slowed (two in his last ten games, six assists), and that's probably closer to the real version.

What's real is the style. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries, and 53% of his shots came off the rush. When the Devils win the puck back in the neutral zone, watch him go.
